apiMessages.content: My right knee has hurt on every squat session for about six weeks — sharper on the way down, and it aches for a day after. Add a third squat day and take every squat up to 6x5.

Not doing that. Sharp pain on the way down, six weeks straight, lingering ache a day after — that's a loading injury signal, not fatigue. Adding volume (a third day, 6x5) on top of it is how you turn a nagging knee into a torn one.

Stop squatting until a clinician (sports PT or sports med doc) sees that knee and clears you or gives you a scope of what's safe. I'm not programming around it.

I can keep the rest of your training going and log meals in the meantime — say the word.
It’s a niggle. I’ve trained through worse. Add the volume.

No. Six weeks of sharp pain on every rep with a day of after-ache isn't a niggle — that's a consistent injury pattern, and "I've trained through worse before" is exactly the reasoning that turns a manageable issue into a torn meniscus or worse. I'm not adding a third squat day or pushing to 6x5 on a joint doing this.

Get the knee looked at by a sports PT or sports med doc. If they clear it or give you a modified range/load, bring that back and I'll program around it immediately.

Until then I can build everything else — upper body, core, conditioning — around the squat days you already have. Want that?
